options_evaluated: Glass-fiber reinforced polyamide (PA6-GF30) with overmolded TPE grips
Monolithic PCR-polycarbonate/ABS (PC/ABS) with detachable mechanical TPU grips
Die-cast aluminum alloy housing with bonded rubber grips
assessments.recommendation: Monolithic PCR-polycarbonate/ABS (PC/ABS) with detachable mechanical TPU grips
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (d) and (p). Avoiding glass-fiber reinforcement and overmolded elastomers prevents contamination of the polymer recycling stream, ensuring high-quality secondary material recovery. Mechanical separation of the TPU grip prevents microplastic and nanoplastic generation during shredding and sorting processes.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Durability/Reliability and Manufacturing. Unreinforced PC/ABS has lower impact and drop resistance than glass-filled polyamide, requiring thicker walls, which increases product weight and tooling complexity.

options_evaluated: Standardized metric machine screws with threaded brass inserts
assessments.recommendation: Standardized metric machine screws with threaded brass inserts
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (c) and (d). Standardized fasteners enable non-destructive disassembly using common tools. This facilitates component harvesting for reuse/remanufacturing and clean separation of metallic inserts from plastic housings at end-of-life, preventing material downcycling.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Manufacturing/Assembly. Threaded inserts and machine screws increase the bill of materials (BOM) cost and cycle time during factory assembly compared to rapid ultrasonic welding.

options_evaluated: Brushed DC motor with press-fit gear assembly
Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with modular, screw-fastened planetary gearbox
Integrated motor-gearbox monobloc with welded casing
assessments.recommendation: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with modular, screw-fastened planetary gearbox
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (c) and (g). Brushless motors have significantly longer operational lifespans due to lack of brush wear, making them ideal for refurbishment and reuse. The modular, screw-fastened gearbox allows separate recovery of high-value copper windings and steel gears, reducing energy and resource consumption in EoL smelting.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Sourcing and Initial Cost. BLDC motors require rare-earth magnets (neodymium) and complex drive electronics, increasing supply chain risks and upfront manufacturing costs.

options_evaluated: Passive aluminum heatsink with removable thermal pads and ventilation
Overmolded fan blades on the motor shaft with dust-filtration mesh
assessments.recommendation: Passive aluminum heatsink with removable thermal pads and ventilation
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (d) and (e). Potting compounds are highly detrimental to recycling as they permanently bond components, rendering PCBs unrecyclable and unrepairable. A passive heatsink with removable pads allows clean, non-destructive separation of aluminum, silicon, and fiberglass.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Reliability/Protection. Potting provides superior moisture and dust ingress protection (IP rating), which protects the tool in harsh construction environments, potentially extending its initial active life.

options_evaluated: Monolithic integrated PCB (BMS, switch, and motor controller on one board)
Highly modular architecture with plug-and-play wire harnesses connecting independent modules
Semi-modular architecture with soldered wire connections between boards
assessments.recommendation: Highly modular architecture with plug-and-play wire harnesses connecting independent modules
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (c) and (r). A fully modular design allows individual faulty modules (e.g., the switch or BMS) to be replaced or upgraded without discarding functioning components, drastically reducing the amount of electronic waste generated during repair and EoL.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Space/Ergonomics and Manufacturing. Plug connectors require more physical space inside the handle, leading to a bulkier tool design, and increase assembly complexity and contact-resistance failure risks.

options_evaluated: Integrated, non-replaceable pouch-cell Li-ion battery pack
Removable and standardized slide-on cylindrical Li-ion battery pack
Direct-wire corded AC power with internal supercapacitor
assessments.recommendation: Removable and standardized slide-on cylindrical Li-ion battery pack
assessments.rationale: Grounded in ESPR Annex I parameters (c), (d), and (e). Removable battery packs prevent the entire tool from being discarded when cells degrade. Furthermore, separating batteries at EoL is critical to prevent thermal runaway/fires in recycling shredders and ensures high-quality lithium/cobalt recovery.
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with Ergonomics and Industrial Design. A slide-on battery pack adds significant weight and bulk to the base of the screwdriver, compromising the compact form factor preferred by users.
